provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: conclusion length differs: the 1962 prints "Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate."; the antecedent prints "qui inter cétera po- téntiz tue miracula, ét"; accents, ae/oe ligatures and word division differ throughout; the antecedent reading is an optical text layer and its pointing cannot be trusted at comma level; content words not recovered from the antecedent layer at this locus (recogniser damage or a dropped ornamental initial): Agathae. Corroboration: 1862 at text-layer lines 73031-73051 (printed p. 530), alignment 0.70; 1604 at lines 56660-56672, alignment 0.73 (degraded-latin; corroboration only). Recorded limitation: The 1962 reading was settled on the facsimile page image; the antecedent reading is an optical text layer only and its letterforms and pointing were not verified on a page image (the 1862's images are not available to this lane, and the Mame's were not rendered for this entry). What was NOT checked: the Benziger conformed printing was used only as a boundary check on the extraction, never as a reading; no attempt was made to establish which of several possible loci in the antecedent is the 'original' one, since an order is not a contribution. The 1 content word(s) listed under differences were not recovered from the antecedent layer; the letterforms there are inferred from the surrounding text and from the other witnesses, not read, so this entry is set to medium confidence. This oration is one the Missal draws from a Common; the antecedent witness may print it at the Common, at another saint's day, or at both. That is a difference of position, not of words.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui inter cetera potentiae tuae miracula etiam in sexu fragili
victoriam martyrii contulisti: concede propitius; ut, qui beatae Agathae
Virginis et Martyris tuae natalicia colimus, per ejus ad te exempla
gradiamur. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit
et regnat in unitate.
